By: Northern Miner Staff November 25, 2026
Australia’s Massive Metals plans to raise up to $40 million (US$28 million) and go public in Canada through a reverse takeover of Argentum Silver (TSXV: ASL) to fund the first drilling since 2008 at its Admiral Bay zinc-lead-silver project in Western Australia.
Argentum would issue 236.9 million shares to Massive Metals shareholders and seek to raise $30 million to $40 million in a brokered private placement before closing, the companies said Tuesday . The share exchange would give the Australian explorer a TSX Venture Exchange listing. Argentum expects shareholders to vote in January 2027.
“We believe this approach has the potential to deliver higher-confidence drill targets and improve the likelihood of intersecting prospective mineralised horizons at depth,” Massive Metals Managing Director Michael Beilby said of combining historical seismic and drilling data with a new geophysical survey.
Previous attempt
The proposed deal renews Admiral Bay’s bid for Canadian financing. Former owner Metalicity pursued a listing for its Canadian subsidiary Kimberley Mining in 2018.
Admiral Bay lies 1,200 to 1,700 metres below surface, about 140 km south of Broome. Historical tests found elevated fluorine in lead and zinc concentrates, which could make them harder to sell.
The companies also disclosed that native title covers the project and no Indigenous land use agreement is in place.
Admiral Bay holds 77 million inferred tonnes grading 4.3% zinc, 3.4% lead and 24 grams silver per tonne for contained metal of 3.3 million tonnes of zinc, 2.6 million tonnes of lead and 59 million ounces of silver, according to an Oct. 6 resource. The estimate uses a US$82-per-tonne net smelter return cut-off.
Canadian mining investor Eric Sprott held 62.2% of Argentum and 14.4% of Massive Metals through companies he controls when the companies agreed to the transaction. One of Sprott’s companies has lent Argentum $750,000 for corporate and transaction costs, according to Tuesday’s statement.
The takeover requires financing, exchange acceptance and approval from disinterested shareholders.
Argentum last traded at 9.5¢ in Toronto before the stock was halted. That valued the company at $4.9 million.

The next EV to plug in at a ski resort might be the one that groomed your trail. ChargePoint has struck a deal with Kässbohrer, the German company behind PistenBully snow groomers, to bring charging to ski resorts and indoor ski facilities across Europe and North America.
Under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers, software, and support with planning, installation, and day-to-day operations. Resorts can use the same provider for the snow groomers and other vehicles they keep at the maintenance depot, as well as for the EV chargers skiers use while they’re out on the slopes.
Kässbohrer’s first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E , uses electric motors to move the machine and spin the tiller that smooths the snow. It has a 196 kWh battery and can handle up to three hours of normal grooming on a charge, according to the manufacturer. It can take up to 22 kW on AC or 150 kW on a DC fast charger. It fast charges from zero to 100% in about an hour.
ChargePoint says Kässbohrer accounts for more than half of the snow groomers sold worldwide each year. Resorts can start working with the companies now. Which resorts will install ChargePoint’s chargers first, and how many will go in, are TBC.

Toyota Hilux Travo Hyper Z Is the Truck We'd All Love To Have
19 photos
Photo: Toyota Thailand
Toyota unveiled the truck that we would all love to have but can never actually get our hands on. It is the Hilux Hyper Z Prototype, called the Travo Z Prototype in Thailand, where it was developed and built in partnership with Toyota Design Australia. The concept looks like it throws caution (and the cargo bed, too!) to the wind.
Unveiled alongside the production Hilux Travo Z Edition at the Toyota Alive in Bangna, Thailand, the Hyper Z is labeled by the automaker as a "Decorative Prototype," specifically designed to inspire Gen Z buyers, aftermarket accessory partners, and potential motor racing projects.
The Toyota Hilux Hyper Z Prototype trades the Hilux's traditional off-road capabilities to become an extreme track- and street racer. It sits low and wide, intimidating and looking fast even when standing still, with a silhouette and add-ons that directly influenced packages such as the Charismo Drit and Charismo Rock factory-backed exterior styling packages.
Development began in 2024 after Toyota designers conducted field research into Thailand’s custom pickup scene, where lowered, street-tuned trucks are hugely popular. Inspired by that culture, Toyota completely eliminated the conventional tailgate and the standard cargo bed to prioritize airflow.
Photo: Toyota Thailand The rear section now houses a massive air intake channel, a prominent Toyota-branded rear wing, aircraft-inspired rear fins, and a large and aggressively styled honeycomb rear diffuser, matching the one at the front, where Toyota came up with a new bumper, pronounced front splitter, and oversized HILUX grille lettering.
Dramatically designed fender extensions widen the double-cab silhouette, while a deep hood scoop makes it look like a hypercar coming from another dimension. The truck, which is no longer an actual truck, rides on massive 22-inch alloy wheels, fitted with white aero-style wheel covers and wrapped in ultra-wide Pirelli P Zero tires, measuring 325/35 R22.
Compared to a standard double-cab Toyota Hilux, the Hyper Z sits nearly a foot (300 millimeters) closer to the ground. It is also a bit longer at 211.0 inches (5,360 millimeters) and wider at 86.7 inches (2,203 millimeters), while standing at 59.6 inches (1,513 millimeters).
The standard Toyota Hilux is 209.6 inches (5,325 millimeters) long, 73.0 inches (1,855 millimeters) wide, and 71.5 inches (1,815 millimeters) tall. The wheelbase remains unchanged at 121.5 inches (3,085 millimeters).
Photo: Toyota Thailand Beneath the ladder-frame construction sits a bespoke motorsport suspension setup with Ohlin remote-reservoir coilovers, Swift springs, upgraded suspension arms, wider tracks, and an easily noticeable negative front camber.
Inside, the standard pickup cabin received a roll cage to keep the occupants safe, a Race Dash digital instrument cluster, a new three-spoke steering wheel, and Sabelt racing bucket seats, equipped with racing-specific yellow harnesses.
Toyota hasn’t mentioned any powertrain details. The Hilux, marketed as the Travo in Thailand, comes with either the 2.4-liter engine producing 147 horsepower (150 metric horsepower) or the 2.8-liter turbo-diesel unit, good for 201 horsepower (204 metric horsepower). But the Toyota Hilux Hyper Z is by no means going into production, so it might as well be displayed with an empty engine bay.

Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV.
Toyota previews its first EREV ahead of Nov 27 debut
The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).
Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.
EREVs use a smaller battery than a pure electric vehicle, while the engine is typically smaller than a PHEV. While they are quieter and often cheaper than a plug-in, EREVs are also less efficient than a pure EV.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
A Nikkei report in September claimed that Toyota was preparing to begin production of its first EREV in China in Spring 2027.
It appears the rumors are true. Toyota’s joint venture in China, GAC Toyota, posted a preview on its Weibo account with the caption #Toyota doesn’t rush but range-extended .
GAC Toyota previews first extended-range EV, a flagship SUV (Source: GAC Toyota)
Toyota didn’t confirm the name, but all signs point to it being the Highlander EREV. The blurry preview looks like the Highlander, and when translated into English, a part of the text below it reads “Cash in on the classics. Global flagship SUV. Not a quick fix, but a range extender.”
GAC Toyota will reveal the new EREV at the Guangzhou Motor Show on November 27. Check back for the full details.
According to the Nikkei report, Toyota aims to produce 200,000 EREVs in 2027. In 2028, it expects production to double to around 400,000 units.
While Toyota likely won’t bring the extended-range EV to the US, it is set to launch the fully electric version of its three-row Highlander in early 2027 (shown above on the left).
The all-electric Toyota Highlander BEV will be available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrains with two battery packs: 77 kWh or 95.8 kWh. The smaller (77 kWh) battery provides up to 287 miles of range, while the larger (95.8 kWh) battery provides up to 320 miles in FWD models.
2027 Toyota Highlander EV three-row seating (Source: Toyota)
Inside, the electric Toyota Highlander EV offers three rows of seating with room for up to seven passengers.
The three-row electric SUV will be built at Toyota’s manufacturing plant in Georgetown, Kentucky.
Electrek’s Take
Like most foreign brands, Toyota is struggling to keep up with domestic brands like BYD, Geely, and Chery in China’s brutal auto market.
However, it’s Toyota’s gas and hybrid cars that are getting crushed by the competition. In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, about 19% fewer than in the same period last year.
After sales plunged nearly 20% , marking its eighth consecutive month with lower year-over-year sales, Toyota said the market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected.”
Toyota looks to avoid the intensifying price war with pure electric vehicles in China. An EREV can potentially be offered at a premium, especially as a flagship SUV.
A company executive said (via Nikkei ) that “Competition in China is intensifying as the market fixates on battery EVs, leading to price wars among automakers,” adding, “We need to take steps to avoid being dragged into that competition.”
Will an EREV help power Toyota’s comeback in China? Or is it late to the party once again? Share your thoughts in the comments.

2027 Bullet Crossfire 234RBK Strikes the Perfect Balance Between Private and Social Activities
15 photos
Photo: Keystone RV Company
There are some travel trailer floorplans that just get it right and with 2027 just around the corner, big-name brands have begun to unveil what they feel is the peak of next year’s designs. If I may, Keystone RV has something quite special ready for us.
It’s called the Bullet Crossfire 234RBK and is one of the latest layouts to join the Crossfire lineup with Keystone RV’s freshest exterior look and upgrades for the class. Personally, I love what they’ve done with this near 28-foot trailer and how it presents itself to potential owners, especially if we consider that it’s often selling for as low as $38K in select dealers.
Photo: Keystone RV Company Now, this is a big camper, at least, in terms of how many people can fit inside. We find access to a modular dinette, a folding sofa, and a “custom” king bed in the bedroom, granting us space for at least six people. That number is cut down to around four with the theater seating option. That’s just part one of the story here.
Part two is how all that’s arranged. Inside the 234RBK, Keystone aimed for the perfect balance between private bedrooms and truly social areas.
Starting with the bedroom, it’s located at the very front of the camper and hidden behind a set of privacy doors. This means that you can hang around in the space all day, and the only moment that you’ll need to come out is for meals or to use the bathroom at the opposite side. Personally, I’d be outside most of the time, but that’s just me.
Photo: Keystone RV Company | YouTube Screenshot The social space, and what makes it so special is up next. Once we step into the camper from outside, the entrance places us right in the middle of the living area; to our right is the bedroom. I liked that Keystone has chosen to place the dinette along the camping wall and immediately across from it, the sofa or theater seating option.
What this does for camper enthusiast is grant them a space where they can dine and chit-chat without having to shout across the camper or even spreading food and dirt all over. Basically, you can invite someone in, plop them down at the dinette, and enjoy. The entertainment center is also in the area, so there’s no need to leave it, all but to go to the bathroom.
Speaking of which, one downside that some owners may be call out is the fact that, to reach the three-piece dry bathroom, which is placed at the rear of the unit, you have to drag your dirt and grime all through the floorspace. Then again, you could leave your shoes and gear outside, possibly hose it down with what dealers are calling, “one of the longest outdoor shower hoses in the industry.”
Photo: Keystone RV Company | YouTube Screenshot As for the very last space in a 234RBK that I want to shed light upon, is the kitchen. One thing to note is that part of the galley is set up on a rack and pinion slide-out that is shared with the sofa or theater seating. This includes the burner, microwave, fridge, and some countertop space and is located along the port wall of the camper.
The rest of the kitchen is located along half of the rear wall and includes a sink with faucet, countertop space, and storage. Yet, what I liked most is the neat little corner view that’s integrated into the shell by Keystone, granting us a view of the world outside from multiple angles.
Just picture this unit backed up toward a lake or some mountain perch overlooking a valley below. Take a moment to see yourself cooking breakfast as you take in the sunrise over the horizon.
Then again, if you want an unobstructed view of the natural world around, you can always head outside like an early bird and set your sights on the outdoor galley that is available in the 234RBK. This feature too, lands on my “like” list and it’s not to be taken for granted as it keeps the spirit of outdoor experiences alive.
Photo: Keystone RV Company | YouTube Screenshot Unlike larger travel trailers on the market, the Bullet Crossfire 2027 234RBK is one of the few that has this outdoor galley in place, and again, is essential for inviting you and the family to experience those moments under a clear blue or star-filled sky, to gather around a campfire, and even hang out under the awning during light summer rains.
Sure, I can talk about the dual AC setup inside, or the washer/dryer prep that is also available, or even the off-grid features, but that’s just frills and all that; what is essential to the class and what it brings to the table in terms of the layout is more important, I’d say.
What does need to be brought to light is the redesigned exterior look for this class – a comparison is visible in the clip from the folks at Apache Village RV Center – the dry weight of 5,980 lbs (2,712 kg) with cargo-carrying capacity of 1,620 lbs (734 kg), the Lippert Road Armor shock absorbing system, built with leaf springs, and the presence of a dual-axle setup. Check out the massive pass-through storage bay at the front.
With 2027 around the corner, we’re bound to keep seeing the hottest campers and travel trailers around, so stay tuned.

Carla Babb is joining Military Times and Defense News as our new Head of Content. In nearly two decades covering national security and international affairs, Babb has earned a reputation for fearless, fact-driven journalism and deep relationships across the U.S. defense establishment.
Recognized as one of the nation’s most candid and well-sourced defense journalists, Babb has broken major stories, pressed senior military leaders for answers and reported from conflict zones around the world. In her new role, she will spearhead editorial initiatives, lead enterprise projects and expand the publications’ presence at major events while developing new ways to engage military, defense industry and national security audiences.
Babb will work alongside Editor-in-Chief J.D. Simkins, who continues to lead coverage by the Military Times and Defense News newsroom. Under Simkins, the newsroom has published its 10 most-read stories of all time within the last year. Simkins was also a recent recipient of the Timothy White Award for Editorial Integrity at SIIA’s Jesse H. Neal Awards. Together, they will lead the next chapter for the brands.
“Carla is one of the most respected and versatile journalists covering national security, and she is the right person to help lead what comes next for Military Times and Defense News,” said Kelly Facer, Senior Vice President at Sightline Media Group, which publishes Military Times and Defense News. “For decades, the military and defense community has trusted these brands to tell them what is really happening. With Carla and J.D. leading our editorial work together, we will build on that trust as we expand into new coverage areas, programs and events for our audience.”
Babb most recently served as national security correspondent for Newsmax and spent more than a decade as Voice of America’s Pentagon correspondent, reaching a global audience of hundreds of millions. She has also reported for Military Times and Defense News.
Babb’s scoops include the 2020 Iranian missile attack on U.S. troops at Iraq’s Al-Asad Air Base, U.S. military interdictions of illicit oil tankers in 2025, and troop deployments and military operations during the 2026 war with Iran. Her interviews with senior military leaders have generated headlines across major national outlets, including The Washington Post, Newsweek, Fox News and NBC News.
“Military Times and Defense News are where service members and their families turn for unvarnished insight and accountability on the issues that shape their lives, and I’m excited about where we can take them next,” said Babb. “I’m eager to get to work with Jon and this newsroom to chase the stories our readers need, widen our coverage and shape national security conversations.”
A prominent advocate for independent defense journalism, Babb serves as vice president of the board of Military Reporters and Editors.
Later this week, Babb will receive the prestigious Prize of Excellence from the Association of Foreign Correspondents in the United States for her outstanding contributions to journalism and distinguished national security reporting. Her work has also earned recognition from the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Foundation, the Press Club of Atlantic City, and regional Associated Press and Society of Professional Journalists chapters.

Hyundai’s All-New 2028 Elantra N Previewed in Realistic Digital Illustrations
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii
The eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra , which is known as the Avante in South Korea, premiered earlier this year, and is already in production, with the assembly taking place in its homeland, as well as in China.
The compact sedan brings sharper overall styling, has a more spacious interior with fresh tech features, and more efficient powertrains. More recently, the company brought it to our shores, where it greeted the public at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show.
Two versions will be sold here, the regular model, with a 2.0-liter naturally aspirated inline-four, rated at 147 hp (149 ps/110 kW) and 132 lb-ft (179 Nm) of torque, and the Elantra Hybrid, with an electrified 1.6-liter four-cylinder unit, and a 1.49 kWh battery. This model has 155 hp (157 ps/115 kW) available via the right pedal combined.
Do you feel like the new-gen Hyundai Elantra deserves to have more power? Well, so does the automaker itself, and as a result, a new generation of the Elantra N is coming. The model is expected to premiere sometime in 2027, and if everything goes right, then it should arrive at US dealers for the 2028 model year.
Mind you, while Hyundai is trying to keep everything under wraps for now when it comes to the upcoming Elantra N, the rendering crowd has started to uncover it. The sporty compact sedan shown in the gallery is a CGI-infused model signed by @avarvarii and shared on Instagram earlier this week.
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii Compared to the regular flavor, the range-topper features an entirely new bumper at the front, with a much larger air intake in the middle, redesigned vents on the sides, and the N logo decorating the small upper grille. It also features side skirt extensions, a more aggressive bumper at the rear, a large wing attached to the trunk lid, and large dual tailpipes.
The pixel artist envisioned it in several colors, and all of them feature red details on the lower parts of the body, and sit on different alloys that are larger in size compared to those of the regular n ew-gen Hyundai Elantra . Expect sports seats on the inside for the driver and front passenger, exclusive trim and upholstery, a different steering wheel, and a few other bits and bobs, too.
The chassis will also be retuned, and the brakes will be uprated in order to keep the extra oomph in check. Rumor has it that the next-gen Hyundai Elantra N could bring a turbocharged 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine, with an alleged 330 horsepower or so. An eight-speed automatic transmission should deliver the power to the front wheels, as an AWD system seems unlikely.

Add a comfortable living room where you can actually entertain, ample storage, and a functional bathroom, and the prospect of downsizing becomes quite appealing.
The Modern Farmhouse tiny home by Sweet-Haus Tiny Cabin Company offers all these features in a package that offers a more generous interpretation of small-space living. At 46 feet (14 meters long) and 12 feet (3.6 meters) wide, this model qualifies as a park model RV and is a perfect example of how downsizing can feel like an upgrade rather than a compromise.
Based in Chesnee, South Carolina, Sweet-Haus Tiny Cabins has been building attractive park model tiny homes that blur the line between traditional houses and mobile dwellings since 2021. Labeled as “tiny cabins,” the company’s models are inspired by Scandinavian aesthetics and are built to the highest standards, with quality materials, excellent craftsmanship, and construction methods typically found in luxury custom homes.
Aimed at people seeking a modern tiny house that allows them to live more simply but still offers generous dimensions, high-end amenities, and exquisite finishes, the Modern Farmhouse offers a spacious floor plan for couples or small families with one downstairs bedroom and an optional loft. Just as its name suggests, this tiny home is designed to offer the comfort and familiarity of a modern farmhouse, and it features open-concept living areas, a seamless flow that makes everyday activities easy to carry out, and natural light throughout.
Photo: Sweet-Haus Tiny Cabins Its generous dimensions and architectural lines give it a more house-like stance than many tiny homes on wheels. However, the main downside related to its size is that it will stay mostly in one place. Perched on a multi-axle trailer, it can still be relocated with special permits and special towing rigs, and you can park it in tiny home communities, RV parks, or on private land.
The home’s exterior gives off contemporary vibes, combining engineered wood siding in a light creamy shade with a dark metal roof. A spacious front porch with thick columns and black wraparound railing sits under a pitched gable roof, further highlighting the farmhouse inspiration. Built directly onto the main frame, the porch features durable Trex decking, stained tongue-and-groove wooden planks on the underside of the roof, and crow’s foot detail under the gable.
It measures 12 feet by 12 feet, so it’s spacious enough to be fitted with dining or lounging patio furniture to create a true outdoor extension of the living space . It’s easy to imagine slow mornings with a cup of coffee in hand or relaxing evenings spent with friends on this generous porch.
Photo: Sweet-Haus Tiny Cabins The 400-square-foot (37-square-meter) interior instantly envelops you in a warm, calming embrace. It exudes modern rustic vibes due to its stained solid-wood ceiling, shiplap walls, handcrafted wooden furniture pieces, and custom millwork for the moldings, window frames, and interior doors. The high ceilings and generous windows make the space feel open and bright, and there are no tight corners to deal with.
A full-light door flanked by large vertical windows opens into the living area, which comes furnished with a sofa, wooden coffee table, and additional seating options. An entertainment wall with space for a TV, an electric fireplace, and a wooden mantel adds a cozy touch to this otherwise modern space.
The gourmet kitchen is another area where the Modern Farmhouse park model tiny manages to dodge the compromises typically associated with tiny homes. Generous in size and properly equipped for full-time living, it’s a space where you can cook all your favorite meals from scratch. Featuring an L-shaped configuration, it offers ample counter space, while floor and overhead cabinets ensure you’ll never run out of space for utensils and supplies.
Photo: Sweet-Haus Tiny Cabins In terms of appliances, it has everything you normally find in a conventional modern kitchen, from a double-basin stainless-steel sink and a two-burner propane cooktop to a large, dual-door refrigerator. It is even equipped with an oven and a small dishwasher. Soft-close doors and drawers, handcrafted millwork, and granite or quartz countertops give the kitchen a refined residential feel.
The Modern Farmhouse is advertised as a one-bedroom tiny home , as it comes standard with just the ground-floor sleeping area, but the featured unit includes two bedrooms thanks to the addition of an optional loft.
Designed to provide comfort, functionality and privacy, the ground-floor bedroom accommodates a double bed with integrated storage, a full built-in closet, and a small desk area that can serve as a workspace. The desk can be replaced by a large dresser, and additional storage is integrated above the bed. The vaulted ceiling is planked in natural timber, which, paired with wooden shelves and worktops, give the room a warm, rustic feel.
Photo: Sweet-Haus Tiny Cabins The secondary sleeping area is located in a loft above the living room, which can be accessed via custom wooden steps. Though it has low ceilings, the loft feels open due to the side windows and can accommodate a double bed and some storage. Next to the stairs there is some extra cabinetry incorporating a washer and dryer. The bathroom offers all the essentials and its styling matches the rest of the house.
All in all, the Modern Farmhouse park model RV offers more space, comfort, and style than most people expect from a tiny home. Pricing for a unit similar to the one pictured here starts from US$126,500, with the final price depending on the materials, finishes, and options selected by the client.

Elecy Velomobile Is Being Tested and Gearing Up To Take On a +18,000-Mile Trip Around the Globe
15 photos
Photo: Amara Automotive
For Decades, the bicycle design has mainly been based around the same look and functionality, and with the appearance of electrification, everything has simply exploded into countless independent disciplines and styles. One of them is velomobiles.
Okay, so velomobiles have been around since well before the electrification of urban mobility, but with the presence of assisted power and batteries that act as fuel, pedaling around in an enclosed cabin that generally adds a whole bunch of weight to your setup, has never been more achievable.
Photo: Amara Automotive Over the years, there have been countless designs that promised to be our go-to and license-free solution for moving around our cities in style and comfort. The whole idea behind a velomobile is to retain the cycling properties that we would find on a bicycle while stepping up comfort and safety.
One way safety and comfort are raised in these vehicles is by using three or four wheels, adding stability and making it rather easy to ride home after a couple of cold ones at a local bar or after a long day at work. Since we’re often placed in a recumbent bicycle position while in a velomobile, that’s even more comfort for you.
Then there’s the fact that these urban mobility machines enclose the rider and sometimes, a passenger too, in a protective shell, often completed from fiberglass or other lightweight composites. Not only does this mean you’ll make it home as dry as a whistle each day, it also means that you’re a bit more protected in case of an accident.
Photo: Trisled Considering the lower stature of velomobiles as opposed to cars, accidents are bound to happen as these low-to-the-ground solutions are harder to see, and if they do, you have that shell ensuring some of the hit is dispersed through the body and frame.
Another trait of a Velomobile, and often, a way of knowing right from the start that its a pedal-powered vehicle, is the body. Since air resistance is a major enemy of cyclists, even more so for vehicles, an aerodynamic shape such as this means you and the motor work less.
Some velomobiles that run no electric components are even more exaggerated in terms of aerodynamic design, with some looking like downright oversized bullets with wheels . Be sure to explore the gallery to see what I mean.
All that brings us to the ravishing machine before us today, the Elecy, a velomobile on which our very own Elena Gorgan shed light upon earlier this year, when the world finally got to see the design in person for the first time. Be sure to check in on that article to grasp a bit more of the backstory for this design and its creator.
Photo: Amara Automotive Now, what Elecy promises is all that I’ve mentioned above, and then some, with the project currently seeing backing from names like Yamaha, the Royal Automobile Club, Royal Commission, and even the Royal Academy of Engineering. The project’s creator, Tamara Ivancova, has her eyes set of an around-the-globe expedition with this thing in 2027, which is just around the corner.
Personally, I understand why all the British groups are supporting the project, but upon seeing Yamaha, I chose to dive deeper into why their name appears. Come to find out, the power behind the Elecy’s assistance is provided by Yamaha. She’s using a PW-X3 motor with a 500 Wh battery that said to be good enough for a peak range of around 80 km (50 miles).
Keep in mind that this is at a top speed of up to 25 kph (15.5 mph), the speed limit over in Europe and the UK, the latter of which being the country where Elecy has been developed.
Photo: Amara Automotive A 14-gear transmission is also called upon, and again, from one of the biggest names in cycling transmissions: Rohloff. You may have heard this name before, and for the Elecy, Tamara has chosen a Speedhub that grants access to 526% of gear range.
What I don’t understand is why Rohloff ISN’t in on this project as a sponsor for the upcoming world tour. I mean, that’s one hell of a feat, and if the gearbox comes out at the other end with no issues, hot damn! Talk about bragging rights. Tamara plans for a 30,000 km (18,641 miles) trip, and the headlines Rohloff could run may be something along the lines, “Can your bicycle gearbox handle 30,000 km?”
The last trait of the Elecy I must bring to light before leaving you to your duties is the fact that Tamara mentions recycled carbon fiber panels as being used in the construction of the shell. It’s also to include a removable canopy, so you can ride around with wind rushing through your hair. There’s space for one adult and one child inside.
Photo: Amara Automotive Toss on an independent suspension system for each wheel, four hydraulic disc brakes, and we have ourselves a bicycle-o-car that, personally, I’d hop into it right now and pedal away on some mountain roads in my area.
At this time, Elecy is actually being tested and has been spotted in several cities across the UK, and if all goes as according to plan, we’ll be seeing this one in the news next time as Tamara attempts the world tour.
PS Wake up Rohloff! Get in on this action and bragging rights.

Six-Grader Saw Rare 1966 Pontiac GTO 4-Speed Tri-Power, Restored It to MCACN Gold Decades Later
44 photos
Photo: Facebook/Marvin's Motor City, Inc.
1966 GTO Tri-Power 4-speed Tiger Gold. Did I get your attention? Undivided, exclusive? Good, because this car deserves it. chances are you might have seen it at the recently concluded Muscle Cars and Corvette Nationals in Rosemont, Illinois. If you skipped it, missed it, or weren’t there, here’s the next best thing – a owner walkaround video.
Few machines radiate pure 1960s swagger quite like a special-order Tiger Gold 1966 Pontiac GTO, and the jaw-dropping example showcased on Marvin's Motor City Garage might be the ultimate rolling time capsule. Owned by Pontiac restoration expert Marvin Minarich Jr. and Kimberly Minarich, this hometown hero blends rock-and-roll attitude with concours perfection.
Returning to the spotlight at the Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals in 2026, it commands attention like a golden-era movie star. Which, let’s be honest, isn’t the easiest thing to do when the house is packed full of greats from all makes and models, past and present. Then again, the Pontiac GTO was never the one to back down from a fight. Especially in 1966.
Its backstory reads straight out of a Hollywood nostalgia script set in Joliet, Illinois, where Gordon Pontiac, Inc. sold the hardtop brand-new. Remarkably, the GTO never left the Joliet area over the past 60 years. As a sixth-grade kid pedaling his bicycle through a newly adopted neighborhood, Marvin spotted the muscular Pontiac parked inside a local garage. He immediately recognized the 4-speed and Tri-Power magic before the house sold and the car mysteriously vanished.
Photo: YouTube/Marvin's Motor City Garage Destiny finally roared back in 2011 when a local enthusiast walked into Marvin's restoration shop after a machine shop recommended him as the area's Pontiac specialist. Visiting the customer's home right in town, Marvin experienced automotive deja vu: sitting before him was that exact sixth-grade GTO. He completed a meticulous concours restoration in 2013 using mostly original sheet metal, original black trim, and rare New Old Stock parts like a genuine NOS throttle cable.
Fresh off the rotisserie, the gleaming Pontiac stormed into the 2013 Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals for a dedicated Tiger Gold showcase, walking away with prestigious Concours Gold honors. It then enjoyed celebrity status on display for several years at the Pontiac-Oakland Automobile Museum in Pontiac, Illinois. After the owner sold it to Marvin's friend, that buyer later needed to fund another classic, letting Marvin finally claim his childhood dream machine for good.
Today, this crown jewel of Marvin's collection refuses to live a pampered life as a static trailer queen. He has joyfully racked up 3,000 miles since its restoration, squealing the tires and unleashing its mechanical symphony exactly as Pontiac’s finest intended. Even better, its provenance is bulletproof thanks to a treasure trove of original paperwork, anchored by an original Pontiac Motor Division dealer invoice gifted by the son of Gordon Pontiac's original dealership owner.
Photo: YouTube/Marvin's Motor City Garage That priceless dealer invoice confirms late-season production at the Pontiac, Michigan assembly plant, carrying an invoice date of July 13, 1966. The hardtop carried a $2,192.91 dealer base cost alongside itemized wholesale figures. Accompanying it is the original window sticker, calculated under the March 16, 1966 federal excise tax rate, proving every dollar spent at the showroom counter.
According to that crisp window sticker, model 24217 (GTO hardtop) began at $2,847, plus a $51 destination charge for a $2,898 subtotal. A roster of ten factory options tacked on $566.75, lifting the final sticker price to $3,464.75. Leading the expense list was the 4-speed transmission at $184.31, followed by the 389 Tri-Power V8 at $115.85, special Tiger Gold paint at $83.20, a pushbutton AM radio at $61.09, and the Safe-T-Track differential at $42.13.
Rounding out the remaining five factory options were ultra-rare front bucket-seat headrests, an original Rally gauge cluster, an outside remote-control mirror, front and rear floor mats. Completing the historical vault is Gordon Pontiac's yellow repair order, stamped “Paid” in January 1967 for $263.45, preserving the original Protect-O-Plate imprint with the VIN and engine code “WS,” alongside vintage "Tiger Town" dealer ads and brochure spreads.
Photo: YouTube/Marvin's Motor City Garage Nothing amplifies this car's pop-culture aura quite like its spring 1966 special-order Tiger Gold finish. Inspired by George Hurst's signature gold wheels—and reborn for 1967 as Coronado Gold—that $83.20 splurge has the same effect in a crowd as a lit lamp at in pitch-black darkness – you can not miss it.
Marvin paired the radiant hue with authentic 1960s Hurst wheels wearing unobtainium spinner caps and redline tires, even re-drilling the trunk lid to mount an eBay-sourced "Gordon Joliet" emblem above his custom frame and GTOTIGR plate.
Pop open the door and the surviving original interior teleports you straight to the mid-sixties. Un-restored black vinyl seat covers, original front and rear door panels, a crack-free dash pad, un-restored Rally gauges, and genuine factory headrests showcase remarkable preservation.
Photo: YouTube/Marvin's Motor City Garage Rather than swapping in a cliché wood wheel, Marvin kept the uncracked factory deluxe steering wheel, while the console-delete floor highlights the chrome shifter, factory locknut-free walnut knob, and a tastefully added period AM/FM radio.
Beneath the scooped hood beats the legendary golden-era heavyweight: Pontiac's WS-coded 389-cubic-inch, 6.4-liter V8, boldly badged “6.5 Litre” (the real displacement was 6,374 cc, just under 6.4 liters).
Featuring a 4.06-inch bore, 3.75-inch stroke, 10.75:1 compression, hydraulic lifters, and three two-barrel Rochester carburetors, this Tri-Power legend unleashes 360 horsepower at 5,200 rpm and 424 lb-ft of torque at 3,600 rpm. Channeling that fury through a wide-ratio M20 4-speed manual and the Safe-T-Track (limited slip, or “Posi,” if you will) axle keeps this 115-inch-wheelbase hardtop composed (sort of).
Photo: YouTube/Marvin's Motor City Garage Fueling Pontiac's all-time GTO sales triumph in 1966—its debut year as standalone series, propelled by Jim Wangers' iconic Tiger ad blitz—production hit a staggering 96,946 units. Hardtop coupes dominated with 73,785 built, dwarfing 12,798 convertibles and 10,363 pillared sports coupes. Tesla has registered a new German company whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.
Neither company confirmed a deal. But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.
What the filing shows
The company is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE. Germany’s official company register lists it under HRB 315756 at the Munich district court, with €120,000 in share capital and a business address of Austraße 24 in Salach, a small town east of Stuttgart. That’s EMAG’s home base.
It didn’t start out as a Tesla company. The register shows it was first entered on August 26 as “Blitz 26-299 SE,” a shell company. Law firms sell these pre-registered shells so buyers can skip weeks of incorporation paperwork, and Tesla renamed this one earlier this month.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Business Insider Germany , which reported the change based on a notice in the federal gazette, says three people run it: Maximilian Stromberger, Tesla Germany’s 33-year-old head of sales, an American robotics engineer, and the head of HR at Tesla’s Grünheide factory.
The HR chief is the interesting name. You don’t need one to hold a passive stake in a supplier, but you do if you’re about to take on employees.
Neither Tesla nor EMAG answered Business Insider’s repeated requests for comment.
Around 220 EMAG workers could move to Tesla
Local press near Salach has been on this for over a week. On November 23, the Stuttgarter Nachrichten reported that signs of a Tesla entry were piling up and that EMAG had briefed its workforce at a large staff meeting the week before. Business Insider dates that meeting to November 16.
Today, the same paper went further. It reports that around 220 EMAG employees will move to Tesla, that the two companies have been working together for some time, and that the deal is about humanoid robots. The full story is paywalled, and none of it has been confirmed by either company.
EMAG builds the machines for robot joints
EMAG, with roots going back to 1867, makes turning, grinding, and gear-cutting machines, mostly for car parts like transmissions and drivetrains. The auto slowdown hit it hard. A year ago, EMAG said it would cut 455 jobs in Germany, roughly 300 of them in Salach, which is about a third of its domestic staff. It lost €42 million on €496 million of revenue in 2024, per Business Insider. It has been talking to potential investors ever since.
But EMAG has also been chasing a new market. Its website has an entire section on manufacturing humanoid robot actuator parts : flexsplines, wave generators, and planetary gears.
The first two make up a strain wave gear, the compact, high-reduction gearbox used in robot joints. Planetary gears go in the bigger joints that carry more load. EMAG says its machines hold these parts to ISO 1328 Class 4 gear quality, with runout under 5 micrometers, and can repeat that in high-volume production.
That’s right where Tesla says it’s stuck. On the Q3 earnings call last month, Musk called the hand Optimus’ main hardware problem and flagged custom gears as a reliability worry, as we reported at the time . Tesla is installing a Fremont line designed for a million robots a year, and the Optimus design it showed in 2022 used 28 structural actuators per robot . At that volume, you’re talking about tens of millions of actuators a year, many of them built around precision gears that few suppliers can make consistently.
Tesla is already building the German side of this. In July, Tesla started recruiting in Reutlingen to develop and manufacture Optimus parts, including sensors, gearboxes, and actuators, plus the equipment to mass-produce them. Reutlingen is the former Manz site that Tesla took over in early 2025 , along with about 300 of its employees.
Tesla’s German shopping list
Tesla has done this before. It agreed to buy Grohmann Engineering in Prüm in late 2016, which became Tesla Automation, and that unit absorbed the Manz operations. Tesla is also putting €3 billion into a Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin .
Tesla briefly acquired Wiferion in Germany. Tesla did buy the wireless charging startup in 2023, but it sold the business a few months later and kept the engineers.

Woman Walks Into a Dealership, Wants To Trade in Her BMW, Won't Take Anything That Starts With an 8
11 photos
Photo: Toronto Auto Brokers | YouTube
A young woman walked into a luxury car dealership in Toronto, planning to trade in her 2025 BMW X5 M60i and hoping to go home with an M4. However, she is a hard bargainer. She won’t take anything that starts with an 8. She paid roughly 120,000 Canadian dollars for her luxury SUV in late 2024 and won’t let it go without a fight.
The one who has to deal with the tough customer, who knows her BMW and what it’s worth, is Gideon of Toronto Auto Traders. She custom-ordered the SUV that rolled off the production line of the Spartanburg factory in South Carolina back in October 2024, and it was delivered later that year.
She seems to have specced it the right way. It is a black-on-white example, which is Black Sapphire Metallic over a Silverstone Sensafin in BMW language. It is definitely a cabin in which future owners should by no means wear dark jeans unless they are transfer-proof.
The BMW X5 M60i is powered by the German automaker's 4.4-liter M TwinPower Turbo V8 engine, paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system. The setup pumps out 523 horsepower (530 metric horsepower) and 553 pound-feet (750 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Toronto Auto Brokers | YouTube That makes it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.2 seconds and max out at 130 mph (209 kph) or 155 mph (250 kph) with max-performance summer tires, because their speed rating safely handles sustained high-velocity heat and extra stress.
For all of these, the owner paid around 120,000 - 130,000 Canadian dollars, which translates to roughly US$84,260 - $91,280. The woman is into sports cars, she has had three BMWs before the X5 M60i, and now she is about to take her fifth home: a BMW M4 Competition. She has a manual M2 and an M340i still parked in her garage.
She says she is upgrading, but is she really? The M4 Competition has no V8 under the hood and has to make do with the 3.0-liter Twin-Turbo inline-six, pushing out 503 horsepower (510 metric horsepower) and 479 pound-feet (650 Newton meters) of torque in a rear-wheel-drive setup or just like the X5 M60i’s V8, 523 horsepower when the all-wheel-drive xDrive system is involved.
The customer doesn't mention which one she wants to go home with, but she is sure of one thing. Her luxury SUV isn't going for anything starting with 8, as Gideon proposes $88,000. She doesn’t even want to hear about it. Instead, she’d prefer a number in the high nines. " I want you to make money, but I want me to make money ," she tells the dealership representative.
Photo: Toronto Auto Brokers | YouTube The SUV is still impeccable and quite low mileage, considering that the odometer reads 27,529 kilometers (17,106 miles) and it won’t even need to undergo the usual inspection because it is still under bumper-to-bumper warranty. Besides, it comes with a long list of interesting options, such as the Carbon Fiber package and the Panoramic Glass Roof Sky Lounge.
The system integrates more than 15,000 laser-etched graphic dots embedded inside the glass panels to create a glowing starry-sky effect at night. She surely won’t get that in the M4. That illuminated panoramic glass roof is reserved for BMW's larger luxury models, such as the X5, X6, X7, 5 Series, 7 Series , iX, and XM.
The M4 Competition , though, is far quicker than the heavyweight X5 M60i. It flashes from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.8 seconds (3.4 seconds for the xDrive-equipped variant) and maxes out at 180 mph (290 kph) when specced with the M Driver's Package. Now, that’s a true sports car.
A clean Carfax, zero accidents, just some curb rash on the rear driver’s side wheel, and two keys, that is what the SUV comes in with. The owner is an insurance broker, working for the second-largest insurance company in Canada, so she knows exactly how much her vehicle car is worth.
Photo: Toronto Auto Brokers | YouTube She says she would be willing to compromise and strike a deal at 95,000 Canadian dollars (US$66,705), but she is ready to drive away if he can’t meet her at 94,000 (US$66,200). Furthermore, she throws in a set of original 22-inch wheels and winter tires, used for only one season. Still, the dealer isn't happy. After tough negotiations, the deal eventually closes at 93,000 Canadian dollars ($65,300).
On the used car market in Canada, such SUVs, with the exact same powertrain, typically sell for between 87,000 and 105,000 Canadian dollars (between US$61,090 and US$73,725), but it all comes down to mileage, factory equipment, and condition.
The insurance broker who just traded in her BMW X5 M60i is also considering selling her BMW M2 with a manual transmission and will probably return to the dealership to trade it in. She hasn’t disclosed what she will be taking home then.

Car Nut Got One-Off Shelby Cobra III Lonestar in '75, Restoration Took 15 Years, He Still Drives It
113 photos
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile
Mike Shoen is the bravest gearhead of our days. He didn’t break any speed records, nor did he scare the devil out of hell with high-adrenaline bravados. But he owns the rarest Shelby car ever. And he drives it. An the street, in normal Arizona traffic. What Shelby, you ask? The Cobra III Lonestar mid-engine supercar. Of which only one was made, and he bought it in 1975.
Ask any gearhead about Carroll Shelby’s glory days, and they will recite the Cobra 289, the brutal 427, and the Ford GT40 by heart. All of them after the glorious Mustang, of course, which is the most numerous of his creations.
Almost nobody mentions the mid-engine marvel meant to replace the sportscars: the 1-of-1 1968 Shelby American Lonestar. Internally called the Cobra III, this blazing-red unicorn recently rolled out on Lou Costabile’s YouTube channel, promptly starting a shouting match with furious Arizona roosters.
The car vlogger just ticked off another unicorn of his list of heroes to get in front of his lenses – he waited four years after spotting the mystery prototype at the Arizona Concours to get together with owner Michael Shoen, who has cherished the one-off for 51 years. He brings the Lonestar to just one show annually, mostly for comedy. Nobody recognizes it, and when he explains its history, skeptics assume he is pulling their leg.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile The plot began in late 1965, when Carroll Shelby was juggling Cobra 427 production, GT40 Mark II re-engineering, European Daytona Coupe duties, and SCCA Mustangs while Ford’s newly installed board members watched every dime. Shelby American’s October 22, 1965 Cobra III proposal budgeted $231,900 for development and $177,000 for tooling.
It envisioned a front-engine car with a 4-speed Toploader or automatic, Ford’s upcoming 351 V8 alongside 289, 427, and 428 options, and—hilariously—a vacuum-formed Royalite plastic body.
Thank goodness Britain intervened before the next Cobra turned into giant Tupperware. English partner John Wyer’s Ford Advanced Vehicles—later J.W. Automotive Engineering—pitched a far wilder plan led by engineer Len Bailey, the mastermind behind the GT40 Mark I and Mark II noses, the street GT40 Mark III, and the higher-performance GT40 Mirage.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Bailey proposed transforming the mid-engine GT40 into a civilized road monster with performance superior to any car on earth. Of course Shelby greenlit it.
There was just one tiny hitch with the name. Ford reminded Shelby that Dearborn owned the Cobra trademark, so the proud Texan thumbed his nose at corporate lawyers and christened the project the Lonestar. While 289 and 427 roadsters cost $6,000 to $7,000 and hit an aerodynamic wall near 165 mph (266 kph), the $15,000 to $16,000 Lonestar aimed straight at wealthy exotic buyers eyeing Lamborghini’s brand-new 172-mph (277-kph) Miura from March 1966 .
That bold mission arguably made the 1967 Lonestar the world’s second purpose-built street supercar, gunning past streetified racers like the 161-mph (259-kph) Porsche 904 and 182-mph (293-kph) Ferrari 250 GTO. Riding a 92.8-inch (2,357-mm) wheelbase—between the Cobra’s 90-inch (2,286-mm) and GT40’s 95-inch (2,413-mm) frames—the simplified tub used 1-inch square steel tubing stiffened with spot-welded sheet metal, mixing Cobra brakes and front hardware with GT40 rear trailing arms.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile In Woking, England, master fabricator Maurice Gomm of Gomm Metal Developments hand-hammered the gorgeous aluminum skin, complete with hinged clamshells and a removable aluminum Targa roof panel that stowed behind the seats. Its lines blend Ferrari P3/4 curves, a Jaguar D-type oval mouth, and a taller, recessed Ferrari Dino-style tail wearing round British Ford rally-sedan taillights.
Period memos budgeted 1,890 design hours and 2,052 build hours, with GT40 knock-off wheels subbing for delayed Cobra Halibrands.
Bailey’s obsession with slicing air paid off big time . December 1966 quarter-scale wind-tunnel tests clocked a slippery 0.36 drag coefficient, calculating that just 295 hp (299 PS) would propel the Lonestar to 200 mph (322 kph), generating 81 lbs (37 kg) of front downforce and 100 lbs (45 kg) of rear lift. Bailey shook it down at Britain’s MIRA track before Wyer’s chief engineer John Horsman drove it straight to the docks for California.
Upon arriving in Los Angeles in mid-1967, Shelby approved the red paint, hated the white interior, and ordered his crew to retrim it in black, tune the 289, and rivet rear-quarter air scoops behind the side windows. Then disaster struck from Dearborn. Dan Gurney and A.J. Foyt had just conquered Le Mans in June 1967, so Ford declared victory over Ferrari, yanked prototype funding, rejected the Lonestar, and pointed Shelby toward Trans-Am Mustangs.
Washington piled on, too. Looming 1968 federal safety rules threatened small-maker exemptions, forcing Autoweek’s 25-cent December 9, 1967 cover—following Scott Malcolm’s November 1, 1967 Road & Track shoot—to warn "Shelby’s New Street Cobra—U.S. Congress Permitting." Its height-compliant bumpers were purely decorative, which Shoen calls a legal joke after working on a 1966 Mustang bumper lawsuit.
Even Shelby shrugged, hating how his tall frame folded like a pretzel over the wide sill fuel tanks. Burned-out and sharp about profits, Shelby knew a $15,000 exotic would bleed money, later cussing the car out to Shoen because it never felt like a real Cobra.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile After posing behind a checkered-dress model on the 1968 Shelby Accessories catalog and touring auto shows, the orphan went up for grabs when Shelby closed his racing shop. In October and November 1968, Al Dowd ran an immortal Autoweek classified screaming "For Sale: Sex on Wheels!!"
Santa Barbara buyer Jeffrey Clark snapped up the $15,000 showstopper, and after changing hands several times, it landed at a North Hollywood used-car lot. In 1975, Gordon Gimbel, who had bought Shelby American’s leftover parts, tipped off Michael Shoen. A former pilot and author of The Cobra-Ferrari War s, Shoen already owned the first Cobra Daytona Coupe—kept for 25 years—and paid a record $15,000 that same year for a four-time FIA-winning works Cobra Roadster.
The Lonestar looked rough enough to scare sane buyers off. It lacked its front bumper, headlight covers, a headlight, and intact glass, sporting rotted fuel cells and a mangled right front fender patched with pop-riveted steel and body filler. Shoen still drove it around Los Angeles, rolled it onto his 1964 competition Cobra trailer—where it fit like magic—and hauled it to Phoenix. Everyone called him nuts except his wife Christa, who instantly adored it.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Christa’s love saved the car twice. When late-1980s money troubles pushed Mike to advertise the battered prototype in Road & Track for $100,000, the phone stayed dead silent, prompting Christa to ban him from ever selling it. Around 2003, Shoen entrusted it to Cobra wizard Geoff Howard at Accurate Restorations in Danbury, Connecticut.
Because Ken Miles and Phil Remington never got to develop the raw prototype, Howard’s marathon overhaul lasted over 15 years—Shoen’s priciest restoration ever.
Wait until you hear how slapdash those British race builders were in 1967. The engine was literally welded—not bolted—to the monocoque, while the transaxle only dropped straight downward after heroic swearing.
Workers aircraft-riveted the aluminum body straight on and buried it in filler, blocking access to the suspension A-arms. Reaching the front wiring meant removing the irreplaceable custom windshield, and nobody could even pour fluid into the brake and clutch reservoirs hidden beneath the cowl.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Howard re-engineered every headache while keeping roughly 95% of the car original before it hit paint in March 2015 and debuted on March 11, 2018 at Amelia Island. He added blind fasteners, Torx screws, swing-out wing-nut fluid brackets, a removable windshield frame with three newly molded windshields, custom Koni shocks replacing extinct Armstrongs, suspension bearings, ATL fuel cells, competition Cobra brakes, aluminum fender repairs.
The restorer hand-formed the steel front bumper from old press photos, and salvaged the bizarre embossed headliner, original shifter, and worn driver’s carpet—patching it with a Cobra-style heel pad—while sanding and polishing Plexiglas windows a past owner had fogged with solvent.
Then came pure slapstick on the first drive . After Howard nervously crept around his local lake, Shoen hit the road and watched the car dart wildly across lanes. Bailey’s improvised tilt column used one sloppy universal joint 6 inches (152 mm) behind the wheel!
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Fine for a golf cart, madness at highway speed—until Shoen and Arizona fabricator Chris Harrison swapped in a solid steering shaft. Behind the cabin sits the original 289-cubic-inch (4.7-liter) Ford V8, punched to 331 cubic inches (5.4 liters) with one Holley four-barrel carburetor and original "bundle of snakes" headers. Paired with a 5-speed all-synchro ZF transaxle, the 2,400-lb (1,089-kg) coupe makes at least 350 hp (355 PS), while period GT40 small-blocks hit 400 hp (406 PS).
Speaking of petty automotive trivia, Ford’s period racers even called their stroked 327 small-block a 325 just to avoid uttering Chevrolet’s famous displacement. To tame Arizona summers, Shoen boxed up the thin steel John Wyer radiator and unneeded heater—hot air already sneaks into the footwells for free—adding a thicker aluminum core and a Bailey-approved GT40 Mark II nose vent.
Street touches include electric windows, generous luggage space beside an FIA spare-tire well, and dual sill tanks. Those sill tanks drain the driver’s side first for balance, and climbing aboard feels, as Mike jokes, like wearing a sock.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Inside, Smiths gauges, toggle switches, and a backup camera pack two adults shoulder-to-shoulder, while Mike drives shoeless on the tight pedals. Out with Lou Costabile, the 331 V8 snarls furiously as Mike laughs off a missed ZF shift, deadpanning about speed limits before admitting he has hit 120 mph (193 kph).
Even after 51 years, the Lonestar’s archive keeps springing surprises. Shoen once found Bailey’s report and a giant box of GT40 records inside Shelby’s closed Princeton building—honestly returning them—and during Costabile’s shoot, they pulled unseen color transparencies from a February 7, 1968 dealer envelope.
One dream remains : re-gearing the ZF, flying Howard to Texas Motor Speedway, and charging past 180 mph (290 kph) toward 200 mph (322 kph) to prove Shelby’s greatest-ever Cobra was truly the first American supercar. And probably the greatest in the whole world back then.

Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa meets US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. ( Image courtesy of Hegseth | X. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 25, 2026
Ecuador has defended its security partnership with the United States after reports that Washington paused joint military operations with the country, where drug gangs are increasingly profiting from illegal gold mining.
Talks last week with U.S. defence chief Pete Hegseth focused on operations and Ecuador’s security needs, Interior Minister John Reimberg told a radio interviewer Wednesday, Reuters reported. He described the discussions as productive, pointing to an established action plan between the two countries.
“Some would like to see these relationships, which have yielded so many positive results, damaged,” Reimberg said.
The New York Times and The Atlantic reported Tuesday that joint operations had been paused. The Times said the halt was in place by mid-October, amid a U.S. investigation into possible human rights abuses during a Sept. 23 Ecuadorian raid that killed a suspected gang leader. The Pentagon told The Atlantic that U.S. personnel didn’t take part in the raid.
Illicit extraction
Illegal mining is among the threats identified in Ecuador’s National Comprehensive Security Plan for 2025–2029. The strategy links illicit mineral extraction to organized crime , money laundering and damage to state institutions.
President Daniel Noboa and Hegseth discussed expanding security co-operation during their Nov. 19 meeting. Noboa did not sign an agreement to continue joint operations, citing domestic opposition ahead of the Nov. 29 local elections, The New York Times reported.
Noboa announced in March that Ecuador would conduct joint operations with the U.S. and other allies, describing the initiative as “a new phase” in the fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining. Ecuadorians voted in November 2025 against allowing foreign military bases on national territory.
Criminal gold
The security plan calls for military operations against illegal mining, seizures of supplies and tighter controls over the industry’s logistics chain.
Criminal groups also use gold mining to launder drug proceeds and finance further operations, according to a June 2025 report by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC).
The research describes weak oversight of processing plants in Portovelo and Zaruma that allows illegally mined gold to enter formal export markets.
Los Lobos extracts gold, extorts miners and controls mine sites and processing plants, the report found. It also identified Guayaquil and Puerto Bolívar as vulnerable points in Ecuador’s gold export chain.
Regional resistance
The Trump administration’s push for regional military co-operation through its Americas Counter Cartel Coalition also faces resistance in Colombia.
During Hegseth’s recent trip, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella told Washington he lacked congressional support to authorize joint military operations, The New York Times reported.
Nearly 70% of Ecuador’s protected areas are located in the Napo province, where most illegal miners are active.
De La Espriella disputed the report , while Hegseth said on X that the alliance between the two countries was “stronger than ever.”
Adam Isacson, a security expert at the Washington Office on Latin America, told The New York Times that the Ecuador pause and Hegseth’s reception in the region suggested Washington’s push for joint strikes was “losing momentum.”
The Pentagon said it remained “committed to working alongside sovereign partners, including Ecuador, to confront narco-terrorist networks,” in a statement reported by The Atlantic .

Tesla Cybertruck Gets $5,000 More Expensive After the Latest Price Hike, and It Makes No Sense
66 photos
Photo: Tesla
Tesla recently announced that the Cybertruck production would stop next summer. This apparently caused a spike in interest toward the weird pickup truck, because Tesla repeatedly raised its price. The latest round saw another $5,000 added to the price of the Cyberbeast, the only variant that is still available to order. This puts the entry price at $114,990, closer to the Foundation Series price but without the perks.
Tesla Cybertruck has always been a slow-selling model after the initial hype evaporated in the first half of 2024. Since then, Tesla could barely sell around 6-7,000 units per quarter, one-tenth of what Tesla thought was possible. Considering the high development costs that aren't shared with any other model in Tesla's lineup, this suggests that the Cybertruck program was losing money.
Unsurprisingly, Tesla decided to cut its losses and announced that the Cybertruck would be retired next year. The move, although highly sensible and also anticipated, left a lot of people speechless. Even Tesla's biggest fans could not get over the fact that the Cybertruck was the third model Tesla axed over the past year, with the Model S and Model X also retired earlier this year.
The Cybertruck's appeal is boosted by FOMO Although the Cybertruck was undoubtedly canceled because it was losing money, Elon Musk vigorously denied it, saying that the Cybertruck was still profitable (God knows how). If that was the case, I fail to comprehend why Tesla would cut such a money maker.
Besides that, Elon Musk is known for having a complicated relationship with the truth. The best example is denying that Tesla's Gen-3 compact EV was scrapped in 2024, even though he knew very well that the story was true .
The funny thing is that a lot of people just realized they wanted a Cybertruck only after it received its last communion from Patriarch Musk. Tesla is usually opaque with its sales numbers, but on the used car market, Cybertruck's prices spiked to new heights, suggesting increased interest.
Photo: Tesla A recent iSeeCars study even placed the Cybertruck as the fastest-selling used truck in the US, spending an average of only 39 days on the market. However, the same is also true for other electric pickups, including the Rivian R1T and the Ford F-150 Lightning. In fact, 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars in the US are fully electric, reflecting a new trend in the market.
Tesla keeps raising the Cybertruck's prices Tesla wants us to think that the new Cybertrucks are just as hot as the used ones, because it keeps bumping the prices after discontinuing the cheaper variants. It had already increased the price when Musk announced its demise earlier this month, with the Cyberbeast starting at $102,490 (+$2,500). Just three days later, Tesla added another $7,500 to the sticker.
Barely two weeks have passed, and Tesla already wants $5,000 more. Obviously, it wants to convey the message that the Cybertruck is the hottest car on the lot. If this is true, the Tesla Cybertruck went from being the Cinderella of Tesla's lineup to, well, still being Cinderella, but after the prince found out that she was the one with the missing shoe.
Forgive me for not buying Cybertruck's sudden popularity. Tesla fans were just as proud to proclaim that the demand for the weirdly-shaped electric pickup was "off the charts" over the summer, when Tesla offered the base AWD variant at $59,990 . However, when the delivery numbers were published, Cybertruck's sales were barely visible in the "Other models" category. I suspect this will happen again when Q4 2026 production and delivery numbers are released in January.
You can't lose money on a truck you don't make If the Cybertruck is really that successful at $115k, why is Tesla stopping production? After all, Musk said that the electric pickup program was not losing money when the Cybertruck retailed for $99,990. With $25k added as a bonus, it should make enough money to be one of the most profitable models in Tesla's lineup.
Photo: Tesla And if it's not actually selling that well, which I believe is more likely, why does Tesla keep raising the price? I'm more inclined to believe that Musk's company is losing a lot of money, and raising the price is just one way of compensating for these losses. After all, there's no economy of scale due to Cybertruck's abysmal sales.
Raising prices is also a way of pushing the potential buyers away. In this case, Tesla signals that it doesn't really want to build more Cybertrucks. You can't lose money on a truck you don't make. And if enough people consider it too expensive, it might just offer Musk another reason to disregard those who asked him to reconsider the Cybertruck's fate.
Among them is one of Tesla's most successful partners, Unplugged Performance. The performance part supplier has asked Tesla publicly to let it build Cybertrucks on its own money. Even better, Unplugged Performance offered to buy the production line and pay Tesla a license fee for every Cybertruck it builds. It also wants to expand the lineup with the famous CyberSUV that everyone wanted and Tesla refused to make.

Rivian R2 and R1 Model Family Recalled for Incorrect Tire Placard Labels
6 photos
Photo: Rivian
Rivian has determined that certain tire placards and certification labels may not describe the wheel-and-tire configurations R1 and R2 customers actually received. A grand total of 1,619 vehicles are being recalled because of this, with Rivian calling this recall FSAM-1900.
Referred to as 26V761 by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the campaign is more serious than it seems. If the recommended inflation pressures are incorrect, over or underinflation increases the risk of a crash. Too much pressure causes the middle of the tire to bulge outward, shrinking the contact patch. Overinflation also means the tire can't absorb bumps properly.
More worryingly, an overinflated tire has no give, making it prone to a sudden blowout. Underinflation is pretty bad as well in this context, for an underinflated tire builds too much internal heat while flexing. Too little pressure also leads to poor handling, for soft sidewalls bend easily when turning the steering wheel. Of course, longer stopping distances also have to be highlighted.
And lastly, improper tire pressures may squeeze the grooves shut instead of channeling water away. This may lead to hydroplaning, and nobody wants that in a vehicle as heavy as a Rivian. Per the recall documentation, the manufacturing dates of the subject vehicles are spread between October 18, 202,1 for the R1T pickup and August 25, 2026, for the R2 sport utility vehicle.
How did Rivian deliver these vehicles with incorrect labels? The automaker's official explanation points to modifications that were made between production and customer delivery. More specifically, a bunch of vehicles may have received a different wheel, tire, and/or spare tire configuration without receiving the corresponding placard information changes.
Photo: Rivian It goes without saying that equipment changes are possible between initial assembly and customer delivery. There's nothing inherently wrong with offering a bunch of configurations, but it sure is wrong when the documentation doesn't keep up with such changes until the first owner takes delivery of the vehicle.
RL00002368-A is the part number for the tire-and-loading label, while RL00000004-D designates the certification label. The recall condition falls under Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 110 for all things wheel and tire selection. Its requirements establish the details that automakers must provide so customers can identify the appropriate tire dimensions, pressures, and wheel setup.
Naturally, the remedy involves replacing the affected tire placard and/or certification label with updated versions containing he correct information. The electric vehicle manufacturer intends to notify customers by January 18, 2027, the day affected VINs are scheduled to become searchable on the NHTSA's portal.
Recently crowned MotorTrend's 2027 sport utility vehicle of the year, the R2 carries a starting price of $44,990 for the Standard, $53,990 for the Premium, and $57,990 for the Performance specification. The latter needs 3.6 seconds to hit 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour), while maximum range favors it and the Premium. Both top 330 miles (531 kilometers) on a full charge.
Not bad for such a boxy vehicle. The R1S can do better still. It goes 410 miles (660 kilometers) at most between charges, while the R1T is listed with 420 miles (676 kilometers).
